en.display_text:
During the Kheda Satyagraha (1918), Gandhi was simultaneously supporting British recruitment efforts for World War I. Which of the following most accurately captures Gandhi's reasoning for maintaining this apparently contradictory dual stance?

(a) Gandhi suspended the Kheda campaign temporarily during periods of active recruitment drives to avoid undermining the war effort
(b) Gandhi treated war support and resistance to unjust revenue policy as separate moral obligations in separate domains — imperial loyalty in the war context did not preclude opposing specific administrative injustices
(c) Gandhi believed that demonstrating Indian military loyalty would directly pressure the colonial administration into granting revenue relief at Kheda
(d) Gandhi conditioned his war support on British withdrawal from Indian internal administration, making Kheda part of that conditional bargain
en.strong_distractor: c — Option (c) is deceptive because students who know Gandhi opposed British policies may assume his Kheda stance also reflected anti-British sentiment in all domains, not recognizing that Gandhi simultaneously supported WWI recruitment — the reversed-causation trap makes conditional loyalty seem contradictory.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (a): Gandhi did not suspend the Kheda campaign during WWI — both ran simultaneously, which is precisely the 'apparent contradiction' the question addresses.
Eliminate option (c): Gandhi's logic was not that the war effort would force revenue relief — he supported the war for separate reasons of conditional imperial loyalty.
Eliminate option (d): Gandhi did not demand British withdrawal from India as a condition of war support — that was the later Quit India (1942) position.

Confirm option (b): Gandhi's logic was that demonstrating loyalty through war support would strengthen Indian claims for political rights, while simultaneously resisting unjust revenue policy — two separate domains of engagement.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Students find it counterintuitive that Gandhi simultaneously supported WWI recruitment and opposed British revenue policy in Kheda. The reversed-causation trap works by offering option (c) — 'war effort will force revenue relief' — which sounds like a logical connection between the two positions. In reality, Gandhi kept the two domains entirely separate: war support was about conditional imperial loyalty and future political claims; Kheda was about a specific unjust administrative policy. The two were not instrumentally linked in Gandhi's own thinking.
en.final_explanation:
The Kheda Satyagraha unfolded while Gandhi was simultaneously supporting British recruitment efforts for World War I — a combination that struck many contemporaries as contradictory. Understanding Gandhi's logic is essential.

• Option (a) — Incorrect: Gandhi did not suspend Kheda to avoid complicating war support — both campaigns ran simultaneously.
• Option (b) — Correct: Gandhi's position was that war support and resistance to unjust revenue policy were separate moral obligations in separate domains. Supporting the British war effort was linked to his theory of conditional imperial loyalty and future political claims for dominion status. Opposing unjust revenue policy at Kheda was a specific administrative injustice, unconnected to the war.
• Option (c) — Incorrect: Gandhi did not argue that war service would instrumentally pressure the government into revenue relief — the two were not linked causally in his reasoning.
• Option (d) — Incorrect: Demanding withdrawal as a condition of support was the 1942 Quit India position — not Gandhi's stance in 1918.

Value Addition:
• The Rowlatt Act (1919) ended Gandhi's conditional British loyalty, transforming him into a full opponent of colonial rule.
• Gandhi's WWI recruitment support was later a source of personal regret, which he acknowledged in his autobiography.
• This dual stance reflects the political complexity of the 1917–19 period — Gandhi was simultaneously building Indian political capacity while operating within imperial frameworks.

• विकल्प (b) — सही: गांधी का रुख था कि युद्ध समर्थन और अन्यायपूर्ण राजस्व नीति का विरोध दो अलग-अलग नैतिक दायित्व हैं जो अलग-अलग क्षेत्रों में हैं। ब्रिटिश युद्ध प्रयास का समर्थन उनकी शर्तीय साम्राज्यवादी निष्ठा और भविष्य के राजनीतिक दावों से जुड़ा था। खेड़ा में अन्यायपूर्ण राजस्व नीति का विरोध एक विशिष्ट प्रशासनिक अन्याय था, जिसका युद्ध से कोई संबंध नहीं था।
• विकल्प (c) — गलत: गांधी ने यह तर्क नहीं दिया कि युद्ध सेवा सरकार को राजस्व राहत के लिए दबाव डालेगी — उनके तर्क में दोनों का कारणात्मक संबंध नहीं था।
• विकल्प (d) — गलत: समर्थन की शर्त के रूप में वापसी की मांग 1942 के भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन की स्थिति थी — 1918 में गांधी का रुख नहीं था।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• रॉलेट अधिनियम (1919) ने गांधी की शर्तीय ब्रिटिश निष्ठा को समाप्त कर दिया, जिससे वे औपनिवेशिक शासन के पूर्ण विरोधी बन गए।
• गांधी का WWI भर्ती समर्थन बाद में व्यक्तिगत पछतावे का स्रोत था, जिसे उन्होंने अपनी आत्मकथा में स्वीकार किया।
• यह द्वैध रुख 1917–19 के राजनीतिक जटिलता को दर्शाता है — गांधी एक ही समय में भारतीय राजनीतिक क्षमता का निर्माण कर रहे थे और साम्राज्यवादी ढांचे के भीतर काम कर रहे थे।

Core Demand and the Revenue Remission Principle

shared.concept_anchor: Rightful resistance peasants using state rules against state

en.display_text:
Consider the following with reference to the Kheda Satyagraha's long-term significance:

Assertion (A): The Kheda Satyagraha exemplified 'rightful resistance' — peasants deploying the colonial state's own administrative rules to demand compliance, rather than challenging the revenue system's legitimacy as such.

Reason (R): Post-independence Land Revenue Codes in India codified the principle that crop failure constitutes legitimate grounds for revenue relief, institutionalizing the very norm that Kheda peasants invoked against the colonial administration.

(a) Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(c) A is correct but R is incorrect
(d) A is incorrect but R is correct
en.strong_distractor: c — Option (c) is deceptive because students who are uncertain about R's claim — that Kheda's remission principle was codified in post-independence Land Revenue Codes — may assume R is fabricated and select (c), when R is historically supportable.
elimination_logic: Step 1: Is Assertion (A) correct? The strategy of using the colonial state's own revenue remission rules to demand relief — rather than challenging the revenue system's legitimacy entirely — is a documented feature of Kheda and is what scholars call 'rightful resistance.' A is correct.

Step 2: Is Reason (R) correct? Post-independence Land Revenue Codes across Indian states did incorporate the principle that crop failure constitutes legitimate grounds for revenue relief — a codification consistent with the Kheda precedent. R is correct.

Step 3: Does R causally explain A? R explains the long-term institutional legacy of the principle that A describes — the fact that the principle was later codified in post-independence law directly validates and explains why Kheda's strategy of 'rightful resistance' was meaningful and enduring. R is the correct explanation of A.
All three steps confirm option (a) — both correct and R explains A.
en.final_explanation:
The Kheda Satyagraha's most intellectually interesting feature was its legal grounding: peasants did not challenge the legitimacy of land revenue itself. Instead, they invoked the colonial state's own remission rule, demanding that the government comply with its own administrative standards. This is what scholars of agrarian history call 'rightful resistance' — using the state's own legal framework as a weapon against its arbitrary application.

Assertion (A) analysis: The Kheda strategy was precisely this — using the colonial revenue rule (remission below one-fourth yield) to make non-payment morally and legally defensible, not just economically motivated. A is correct.

Reason (R) analysis: Post-independence Land Revenue Codes in several states — particularly Gujarat's own revenue legislation — incorporated the principle that crop failure and natural calamity constitute grounds for revenue relief. This is a direct institutional legacy of the Kheda principle. R is correct.

Causal relationship: R explains A — the lasting codification of the remission principle validates that Kheda's 'rightful resistance' strategy was not merely tactical but established a genuine administrative norm that survived colonial rule. R directly explains why A's characterization of Kheda is accurate.

Value Addition:
• 'Rightful resistance' as an academic framework (associated with Kevin O'Brien's work on China, applied to India by agrarian historians) examines how peasants use state norms against state abuse.
• Kheda's precedent influenced Zamindari Abolition moral framing: peasants have rights against arbitrary state extraction.
• Patel's administrative style as Home Minister — combining firmness with recognition of legitimate grievances — arguably reflected his Kheda experience.

कथन (A): खेडा सत्याग्रह 'वैध प्रतिरोध' का उदाहरण था — किसानों ने उपनिवेशी राज्य के अपने प्रशासनिक नियमों का उपयोग अनुपालन की मांग के लिए किया, न कि राजस्व प्रणाली की वैधता को चुनौती देने के लिए।

कारण (R): स्वतंत्रता के बाद भारत की भूमि राजस्व संहिताओं में यह सिद्धांत संहिताबद्ध किया गया कि फसल विफलता राजस्व राहत के लिए वैध आधार है, जो उस मानदंड को संस्थागत बनाता है जिसका खेडा के किसान उपनिवेशी प्रशासन के खिलाफ उपयोग करते थे।

(a) A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है
(b) A और R दोनों सही हैं परंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
(c) A सही है परंतु R गलत है
(d) A गलत है परंतु R सही है
hi.strong_distractor: c — विकल्प (c) भ्रमित करने वाला है क्योंकि जो छात्र R के दावे — कि खेडा का माफी सिद्धांत स्वतंत्रता के बाद के भूमि राजस्व संहिता में संहिताबद्ध किया गया था — के बारे में अनिश्चित हैं, वे मान सकते हैं कि R काल्पनिक है और (c) चुन सकते हैं, जबकि R ऐतिहासिक रूप से समर्थनीय है।
elimination_logic: चरण 1: क्या कथन (A) सही है? उपनिवेशी राज्य के अपने राजस्व माफी नियमों का उपयोग राहत मांगने के लिए करना — राजस्व प्रणाली की वैधता को पूरी तरह चुनौती देने के बजाय — खेडा की एक प्रलेखित विशेषता है और इसे विद्वान 'वैध प्रतिरोध' कहते हैं। A सही है।

चरण 3: क्या R, A की कारणात्मक व्याख्या करता है? ये तीनों चरण विकल्प (a) की पुष्टि करते हैं — दोनों सही हैं और R, A की व्याख्या करता है।
hi.final_explanation:
खेडा सत्याग्रह की सबसे बौद्धिक रूप से रोचक विशेषता इसका कानूनी आधार था: किसानों ने भूमि राजस्व की वैधता को चुनौती नहीं दी। इसके बजाय, उन्होंने उपनिवेशी राज्य के अपने माफी नियम का हवाला दिया, सरकार से अपने प्रशासनिक मानकों का पालन करने की मांग की। इसे कृषि इतिहास के विद्वान 'वैध प्रतिरोध' कहते हैं — राज्य के अपने कानूनी ढांचे का उपयोग उसके मनमाने प्रयोग के खिलाफ हथियार के रूप में।

कथन (A) का विश्लेषण: खेडा की रणनीति बिल्कुल यही थी — उपनिवेशी राजस्व नियम (फसल के एक-चौथाई से कम होने पर माफी) का उपयोग करके गैर-भुगतान को नैतिक और कानूनी रूप से सही ठहराना, केवल आर्थिक प्रेरित नहीं। A सही है।

कारण (R) का विश्लेषण: स्वतंत्रता के बाद कई राज्यों की भूमि राजस्व संहिताओं — विशेष रूप से गुजरात की अपनी राजस्व विधान — में यह सिद्धांत शामिल किया गया कि फसल विफलता और प्राकृतिक आपदा राजस्व राहत के आधार हैं। यह खेडा सिद्धांत की प्रत्यक्ष संस्थागत विरासत है। R सही है।

• 'वैध प्रतिरोध' एक शैक्षणिक ढांचा है (जो केविन ओ'ब्रायन के चीन पर कार्य से जुड़ा है, जिसे भारत में कृषि इतिहासकारों ने लागू किया) जो यह जांचता है कि किसान राज्य के नियमों का उपयोग राज्य के दुरुपयोग के खिलाफ कैसे करते हैं।
• खेडा का उदाहरण जमींदारी उन्मूलन के नैतिक ढांचे को प्रभावित करता है: किसानों के पास मनमाने राज्य शोषण के खिलाफ अधिकार हैं।
• गृह मंत्री के रूप में पटेल की प्रशासनिक शैली — दृढ़ता के साथ वैध शिकायतों की मान्यता का संयोजन — संभवतः उनके खेडा अनुभव को दर्शाती है।

shared.concept_anchor: Kheda dual crisis trigger conditions 1917-18

en.display_text:
With reference to the background and trigger conditions of the Kheda Satyagraha (1918), consider the following statements:

1. The immediate crisis that triggered the Kheda Satyagraha involved both an agricultural shock — floods and drought in 1917–18 — and a public health emergency in the form of a plague epidemic.
2. The Kheda Satyagraha was rooted in grievances over forced indigo cultivation imposed by British planters on Kheda district's peasants.
3. The British administration's refusal to acknowledge crop failure data presented by peasants, combined with the government's own surveys claiming yield was above the remission threshold, created a clash between ground reality and official data at Kheda.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: The immediate crisis that triggered the Kheda Satyagraha involved both an agricultural shock — floods and drought in 1917–18 — and a public health emergency in the form of a plague epidemic.
statement_analysis.reason: Historical accounts of Kheda consistently identify the dual crisis — crop failure due to flooding and drought combined with a plague epidemic — as the conditions that made the revenue demand acutely unjust and triggered the satyagraha.

statement_analysis.statement: The Kheda Satyagraha was rooted in grievances over forced indigo cultivation imposed by British planters on Kheda district's peasants.
statement_analysis.reason: Forced indigo cultivation under the tinkathia system was the Champaran grievance, not Kheda's. Kheda's dispute was entirely about colonial government revenue demands during a period of crop failure — private planters had no role.

statement_analysis.statement: The British administration's refusal to acknowledge crop failure data presented by peasants, combined with the government's own surveys claiming yield was above the remission threshold, created a clash between ground reality and official data at Kheda.
statement_analysis.reason: The British counter-argument was precisely that its own surveys showed yields above the one-fourth threshold, directly contradicting peasant accounts — this data vs. ground reality clash was central to the moral case for satyagraha.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option (d) is deceptive because all three statements may appear plausible to a student who conflates Champaran and Kheda conditions, and accepting Statement 2 as broadly about 'planter exploitation' leads to selecting all three as correct.
elimination_logic: Verify Statement 2: Indigo/planter grievances are definitionally Champaran's issue — Kheda had no indigo or planter involvement. Statement 2 is incorrect; eliminate options containing Statement 2.
Verify Statement 1: Dual crisis (floods/drought + plague) is historically documented as Kheda's trigger. Statement 1 is correct.
Verify Statement 3: The government's survey-based counter-argument vs. peasant ground reality is a documented feature of the Kheda dispute. Statement 3 is correct.
Option (b) — Statements 1 and 3 — is the correct answer.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 is a direct conflation trap — it inserts the Champaran grievance (forced indigo cultivation by planters) into a question about Kheda, which had no planter involvement whatsoever. Students who have studied both movements but not internalized their distinct adversaries will accept Statement 2 as 'approximately correct' because it describes real British-era peasant exploitation. The trap is especially effective because the other two statements are clearly correct, making a student want to include Statement 2 to reach 'all three' and select option (d).
en.final_explanation:
The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) had a specific, historically precise set of trigger conditions — not a generic agrarian crisis.

• Statement 1 — Correct: The dual crisis of crop failure (floods, drought) in 1917–18 combined with a plague epidemic created acute rural distress in Kheda district, making the continued revenue demand morally indefensible.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: Forced indigo cultivation was the Champaran (Bihar) grievance against private European planters. Kheda's adversary was the colonial revenue administration. No indigo or planter issue existed in Kheda.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The core conflict at Kheda was between peasant-reported ground reality (yield well below one-fourth) and the government's own survey data claiming yields were above the remission threshold. This 'clash of data' gave Gandhi the moral high ground — demanding the state apply its own standard consistently.

Value Addition:
• The distinction 'private planter adversary (Champaran) vs. colonial state adversary (Kheda)' is the most frequently tested comparative fact about Gandhi's early campaigns.
• The British use of official survey data to override ground-level evidence was a broader feature of colonial administrative practice, not unique to Kheda.
• The plague epidemic dimension of Kheda is often omitted in standard accounts — it is a UPSC-relevant distinguishing detail.

en.display_text:
Historian Sumit Sarkar and others have raised questions about whether the Kheda Satyagraha represented genuine mass mobilization or served a narrower sectional interest. The primary basis of this historiographical critique is:

(a) The movement's failure to spread beyond Kheda district to adjacent regions of Gujarat
(b) The geographic confinement of the campaign, which prevented landless laborers in other districts from participating
(c) The ambiguous outcome — the absence of formal revenue remission legislation — which suggested the movement failed its stated objectives
(d) The movement's class composition — it was dominated by Patidar landowning peasants while landless laborers and artisans were largely excluded, raising questions about whose interests it truly served
en.strong_distractor: b — Option (b) is deceptive because it correctly identifies class limitation as a critique but attributes it to geographic spread failure — conflating the class critique (who participated) with the geographic critique (where it spread), two distinct but related limitations.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (a): Geographic confinement to Kheda district is a real limitation, but the historiographical debate associated with Sumit Sarkar specifically concerns class representation, not geographic spread.
Eliminate option (b): Class limitation and geographic limitation are distinct critiques — option (b) conflates them.
Eliminate option (c): The outcome ambiguity critique (no formal legislation) is a real limitation but is not the primary basis of Sumit Sarkar's 'genuine mass mobilization' question.

Confirm option (d): Sarkar's critique centers on whether Kheda represented broad mass mobilization or the protection of elite Patidar landed interests — the class composition question is the correct characterization of this historiographical debate.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Option (b) is designed to trap students who know both critiques of Kheda — class limitation and geographic limitation — but conflate them when asked specifically about the 'genuine mass mobilization' debate. Sumit Sarkar's question is precisely whether the Patidar-dominated movement represented genuine peasant mass mobilization or elite landed interest protection. The geographic limitation is a separate, less philosophically charged critique. Confusing the two demonstrates surface-level knowledge without analytical precision.
en.final_explanation:
The Kheda Satyagraha has generated significant historiographical debate about its representativeness. Scholars like Sumit Sarkar have questioned whether it constituted genuine mass mobilization or primarily served the interests of a dominant peasant group.

• Option (a) — Incorrect: Geographic confinement is a real limitation, but not the basis of the 'genuine mass mobilization' question Sarkar raises.
• Option (b) — Incorrect: This conflates the class critique with a geographic spread argument — they are distinct limitations.
• Option (c) — Incorrect: Outcome ambiguity (no formal legislation) is a valid criticism but relates to outcomes, not to who participated or whose interests were served.
• Option (d) — Correct: Sarkar's critique is specifically about class composition — the movement was dominated by Patidars (a prosperous landowning community), while landless laborers and artisans were largely excluded. This raises the question of whether it represented broad peasant interests or elite peasant interest protection.

Value Addition:
• The Patidar community's political mobilization through Kheda and Bardoli laid the foundation for Gujarat's distinctive political culture.
• Sarkar's critique is part of a broader 'subaltern studies' debate about whether nationalist-era agrarian movements served elite or genuinely popular interests.
• Landless laborers — excluded from Kheda — were not addressed until later legislation like Zamindari Abolition.

(a) आंदोलन का खेडा जिले से बाहर गुजरात के आस-पास के क्षेत्रों में फैलने में विफल होना

(d) आंदोलन की वर्ग संरचना — यह पाटीदार जमींदार किसानों द्वारा प्रभुत्वशाली था जबकि भूमिहीन मजदूर और कारीगर अधिकांशतः बाहर थे, जिससे यह प्रश्न उठता है कि यह वास्तव में किसके हितों की सेवा करता था

• विकल्प (c) — गलत: परिणाम अस्पष्टता (कोई औपचारिक कानून नहीं) एक वैध आलोचना है लेकिन यह परिणामों से संबंधित है, न कि यह कि कौन भाग लिया या किसके हितों की सेवा हुई।

en.strong_distractor: a — Option (a) — Champaran — is deceptive because Champaran was indeed Gandhi's first major Indian satyagraha, and students conflate 'first' with 'first major peasant revenue satyagraha,' missing that the Ahmedabad Mill Strike was a separate labor dispute and that Kheda was specifically the first revenue non-payment campaign.

Eliminate option (b): Bardoli (1928) was a direct revenue non-payment campaign but occurred ten years after Kheda — it cannot be 'first.'
Eliminate option (d): The Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919) was about emergency detention legislation, not peasant revenue grievances at all.

Confirm option (c): Kheda (1918) was Gandhi's first direct confrontation with colonial revenue demands — a peasant satyagraha involving the state as adversary, unlike Champaran's planter-adversary structure.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Option (a) — Champaran — is the intended trap. Champaran is correctly identified as Gandhi's 'first major Indian satyagraha' and students anchor 'first' to it reflexively. The question, however, specifies 'peasant revenue satyagraha involving direct confrontation with the colonial state's revenue administration' — a characterization that excludes Champaran (which targeted private planters) and identifies Kheda precisely. en.final_explanation:
Precision about what each Gandhi campaign represented is essential for UPSC.

• Option (a) — Champaran: Incorrect. Champaran (1917) was Gandhi's first Indian satyagraha overall, but it confronted private indigo planters over the tinkathia system — not the colonial state's revenue administration. The adversary distinction makes Champaran incorrect here.
• Option (b) — Bardoli: Incorrect. Bardoli (1928) was a structurally identical revenue campaign but came a full decade after Kheda — it cannot be 'first.'
• Option (c) — Kheda: Correct. Kheda (1918) was Gandhi's first peasant satyagraha in which the colonial state's revenue administration was the direct adversary — a fiscally and administratively grounded confrontation different in character from Champaran.
• Option (d) — Rowlatt Satyagraha: Incorrect. Rowlatt (1919) addressed emergency detention legislation — entirely different from peasant revenue grievances.

Value Addition:
• The Champaran-Kheda distinction — private adversary vs. state adversary — is the single most important comparative fact about Gandhi's early campaigns.
• Bardoli (1928) is sometimes called 'Kheda completed' because it achieved what Kheda could not: a formal government concession.
• All three — Champaran, Kheda, Ahmedabad Mill Strike — were Gandhi's 'laboratories' for distinct methods applied to different social classes.

en.display_text:
Which of the following pairs correctly matches a Gandhi-led agrarian campaign with its actual formal outcome?

(a) Kheda Satyagraha (1918) — Enactment of the Kheda Peasants' Relief Act (1918) granting statutory revenue remission to affected cultivators
(b) Kheda Satyagraha (1918) — Passage of the Champaran Agrarian Act (1918) abolishing forced cultivation contracts
(c) Kheda Satyagraha (1918) — Appointment of the Broomfield-Maxwell inquiry committee to review the revenue assessment
(d) Kheda Satyagraha (1918) — An informal administrative instruction to revenue collectors to recover dues only from those peasants who demonstrably had the means to pay, with no formal written order issued
en.strong_distractor: b — Option (b) is deceptive because it correctly identifies Kheda as the movement where no formal legislation resulted, but misattributes to it the Champaran Agrarian Act (1918) as the outcome, creating a plausible-sounding pair that reverses the correct attribution.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (a): Kheda did not produce formal legislation — attributing a 'Kheda Peasants' Relief Act (1918)' to it is a fabrication.
Eliminate option (b): The Champaran Agrarian Act (1918) belongs to Champaran, not Kheda — this is a direct entity-swap.
Eliminate option (c): The Bardoli inquiry (Broomfield-Maxwell) belongs to Bardoli (1928), not Kheda (1918) — temporal-swap.

Confirm option (d): Kheda's resolution was an informal, unwritten instruction to revenue collectors to recover dues only from those who could pay — no formal written order or legislation, correctly paired with Kheda.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Option (b) is the primary trap: it correctly identifies 'Kheda' in the pair but attributes the Champaran Agrarian Act (1918) to it — a real piece of legislation from the correct year, making the pair sound plausible. Students who know 1918 produced important agrarian legislation may not remember which movement produced which outcome, and the same year (1918) for both Champaran's legislation and Kheda's campaign creates maximum confusion. This is a temporal-swap combined with entity-swap.
en.final_explanation:
The outcomes of Gandhi's early Indian satyagrahas are as important as their methods. Champaran and Kheda both concluded in 1918 but with radically different formal results.

• Option (a) — Incorrect: 'Kheda Peasants' Relief Act (1918)' does not exist — Kheda produced no legislation whatsoever. This is a plausible-fabrication.
• Option (b) — Incorrect: The Champaran Agrarian Act (1918) abolished the tinkathia system — it belongs to Champaran, not Kheda. Attributing it to Kheda swaps the two movements' outcomes.
• Option (c) — Incorrect: The Broomfield-Maxwell inquiry belongs to Bardoli (1928), not Kheda (1918) — a decade-long temporal-swap.
• Option (d) — Correct: Kheda's resolution was genuinely informal — the government gave revenue collectors an oral/administrative instruction to recover dues only from those who demonstrably could pay, leaving the genuinely distressed. No binding written order was issued.

Value Addition:
• Champaran produced formal legislation (Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918); Kheda produced only an informal administrative instruction — the contrast defines their comparative UPSC significance.
• Gandhi declared Kheda a 'moral victory' precisely because no formal concession was obtained — the declaration was strategic, not merely rhetorical.
• Bardoli (1928) closed the loop — it achieved the formal inquiry and concession that Kheda could not.

गांधी के प्रारंभिक भारतीय सत्याग्रहों के परिणाम उनके तरीकों जितने ही महत्वपूर्ण हैं। चंपारण और खेडा दोनों 1918 में समाप्त हुए लेकिन उनके औपचारिक परिणाम पूरी तरह भिन्न थे।

(b) Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(c) A is correct but R is incorrect
(d) A is incorrect but R is correct
en.strong_distractor: a — Option (a) is deceptive because students may assume that if Gandhi chose caution about women's participation (R), it must be because he was responding to social conservatism (a valid reason), making R appear to explain A directly — but R states the wrong causal factor (Gandhi's 'own cautious approach at this stage') when both Gandhi's approach AND social conservatism were factors.
elimination_logic: Step 1: Is Assertion (A) correct? Women's participation at Kheda was limited — this is historically documented; large-scale women's mobilization came in 1930 and 1942. A is correct.

Step 2: Is Reason (R) correct? Gandhi's cautious approach to women's mass mobilization at the 1918 stage of his Indian career is documented — he gradually expanded women's roles across successive campaigns. R is correct.

Step 3: Does R causally explain A? R identifies Gandhi's own approach as the reason, but the complete causal picture at Kheda includes both Gandhi's caution AND the social conservatism of rural Gujarat in 1918. R is a contributing cause but does not constitute the complete explanation of A — additionally, R attributes limited participation purely to Gandhi's choice, obscuring the structural social factors. The explanation is incomplete rather than wrong. However, R does provide a genuine partial causal explanation that is factually correct — best categorized as (b): both correct but R is not the complete/correct explanation.
Final step names option (b) — matching correct_option (b).
en.final_explanation:
Women's participation in the Kheda Satyagraha was limited compared to the mass mobilization of later campaigns. Understanding why requires separating multiple contributing factors.

Assertion (A) analysis: Limited women's participation at Kheda is well-documented. Women's documented roles — preventing cattle auctions, maintaining household solidarity — were important but small-scale, far from the mass picketing and public demonstrations of the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930). A is correct.

Reason (R) analysis: Gandhi did take a cautious approach to women's mass mobilization in 1918 — this evolved across his Indian campaigns. His approach became progressively more inclusive: Non-Cooperation (1920), then Civil Disobedience (1930), then Quit India (1942) each saw expanded women's roles. R is factually correct.

Causal relationship: R identifies Gandhi's own caution as the reason, which is a genuine contributing factor. However, the complete causal explanation for Kheda's limited women's participation also requires acknowledging the social conservatism of rural Gujarat in 1918 — an independent structural constraint. R is true but incomplete as an explanation, making it not the 'correct' complete explanation of A.

Value Addition:
• Women's role at Kheda — preventing auction interference — was an early form of non-violent direct action that later scaled massively.
• The progression of women's participation across Gandhi's campaigns (Kheda → Non-Cooperation → Civil Disobedience → Quit India) is itself a UPSC-testable chronological pattern.
• Rural Gujarat's social conservatism in 1918 was a structural constraint independent of Gandhi's own approach.

खेड़ा सत्याग्रह में महिलाओं की भागीदारी बाद के अभियानों की जनसामूहिक भागीदारी की तुलना में सीमित थी। इसके कारणों को समझने के लिए कई सहायक कारकों को अलग करना आवश्यक है।

• खेड़ा में महिलाओं की भूमिका — नीलामी में हस्तक्षेप रोकना — अहिंसात्मक प्रत्यक्ष कार्रवाई का एक प्रारंभिक रूप था जो बाद में बड़े पैमाने पर हुआ।

Three of the following four campaigns share a common structural feature. Which one does NOT belong to the same category as the others?

(a) Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918)
(b) Champaran Satyagraha (1917)
(c) Kheda Satyagraha (1918)
(d) Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)
en.strong_distractor: c — Option (c) — Kheda Satyagraha — is deceptive because Kheda is the most famous of Gandhi's 1918 campaigns and students may assume it is being tested as the 'exceptional' case for some other reason, failing to notice that Ahmedabad is the structural odd-one-out.
elimination_logic: Identify the common attribute: Champaran, Kheda, and Bardoli were all agrarian/peasant revenue campaigns — they addressed land, cultivation contracts, or government revenue assessment.

Test Ahmedabad Mill Strike against this attribute: Ahmedabad (1918) was an urban industrial labor dispute between textile mill workers and mill owners over wages — structurally unrelated to land, cultivation, or revenue.
Kheda, Champaran, and Bardoli all fit the 'peasant agrarian campaign' category; Ahmedabad does not.
Option (a) — Ahmedabad Mill Strike — is the odd one out.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The conflation trap here works because Ahmedabad (1918) and Kheda (1918) occurred in the same year and region (Gujarat), making students associate them as similar 'Gujarat 1918' events. Students who think in terms of 'Gandhi's 1918 campaigns' as a category will include Ahmedabad as part of the peasant movement cluster. The precise distinction — urban labor (Ahmedabad) vs. rural agrarian (Kheda, Champaran, Bardoli) — is what separates a correct from incorrect answer. Bardoli's inclusion as a plausible answer is a second-level trap for students who might think 'Bardoli is 1928, not a peasant movement' — it is in fact a revenue movement and belongs with the agrarian category.
en.final_explanation:
This question requires identifying the structural category that unites three of the four options.

• Option (a) — Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918): The odd one out. This was an urban industrial labor dispute — textile mill workers demanding a 35% wage increase from mill owners. It had no agrarian, land, or revenue dimension.
• Option (b) — Champaran Satyagraha (1917): An agrarian campaign against the tinkathia forced cultivation system — fits the peasant/agrarian category.
• Option (c) — Kheda Satyagraha (1918): An agrarian campaign against colonial land revenue demands — fits the peasant/agrarian category.
• Option (d) — Bardoli Satyagraha (1928): An agrarian revenue non-payment campaign — fits the peasant/agrarian category.

The common attribute: Champaran, Kheda, and Bardoli were all campaigns involving land, cultivation, or government revenue assessment in rural agricultural settings. Ahmedabad was exclusively an urban industrial labor dispute.

Value Addition:
• Gandhi managed the Ahmedabad Mill Strike and Kheda Satyagraha nearly simultaneously in 1918 — he fasted during the Mill Strike to support workers.
• Ahmedabad was unusual in Gandhi's career: he was mediating between industrialists (who were his financial supporters) and workers.
• The Ahmedabad Mill Strike established Gandhi's credibility with urban labor, distinct from his agrarian constituency.

• विकल्प (d) — बारडोली सत्याग्रह (1928): कृषि राजस्व न भुगतान अभियान — किसान/कृषि श्रेणी में आता है।

shared.concept_anchor: British distraint strategy movable property not land

en.display_text:
With reference to the British administrative response to the Kheda Satyagraha (1918), consider the following statements:

1. The British administration specifically targeted movable assets — cattle, agricultural implements, and standing crops — for attachment and auction, deliberately avoiding direct action against land.
2. British coercive measures during Kheda proved highly effective, as the threat of cattle auction caused a majority of Patidar households to resume revenue payments within the first month of enforcement.
3. The failure of British coercive measures at Kheda illustrated a pattern in which state-imposed pressure on communities practising collective non-compliance paradoxically reinforced solidarity rather than inducing defection.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: The British administration during the Kheda Satyagraha specifically targeted movable assets — cattle, agricultural implements, and standing crops — for attachment and auction, deliberately avoiding direct action against land.
statement_analysis.reason: This selective distraint strategy was a deliberate colonial calculation: attacking land would fuel a larger and more dangerous rebellion, while targeting movable assets seemed a proportionate coercive response likely to force compliance without expanding the conflict.

statement_analysis.statement: British coercive measures during Kheda proved highly effective, as the threat of cattle auction caused a majority of Patidar households to resume revenue payments within the first month of enforcement.
statement_analysis.reason: British coercion at Kheda was documented as ineffective — peasants hid assets before revenue officers arrived, and neighbors refused to bid at auctions, rendering the distraint strategy counterproductive. Paradoxically, coercion strengthened rather than broke peasant solidarity.

statement_analysis.statement: The failure of British coercive measures at Kheda illustrated a pattern in which state-imposed pressure on communities practicing collective non-compliance paradoxically reinforced solidarity rather than inducing defection.
statement_analysis.reason: This dynamic — coercion strengthening collective action — is documented at Kheda and recurred in Bardoli (1928) and other satyagrahas. When all members faced common threat, individual defection became socially costly, sustaining collective resistance.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option (d) is deceptive because Statement 3's academic-sounding language about 'paradoxical reinforcement of solidarity' may strike students as an over-interpretation, leading them to reject it and select only Statement 1 as correct — option (a).
elimination_logic: Verify Statement 1: Selective targeting of movable property to avoid land seizure is historically documented as a deliberate British strategy at Kheda — correct.
Verify Statement 2: British coercion at Kheda was NOT effective — auctions failed because of asset concealment and neighbor solidarity. The 'majority resumed payment' claim is false — mark incorrect.
Verify Statement 3: The coercion-strengthens-solidarity dynamic is documented at Kheda and is consistent with the broader historical record of similar movements. Statement 3 is correct.
Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 is a direct reversal of what happened at Kheda — British coercion failed spectacularly, strengthening rather than breaking solidarity. Students who recall that the British 'did try coercion' may not remember whether it succeeded, and the confident language ('majority resumed payment within the first month') sounds authoritative. Statement 3's academic framing may cause students to doubt its factual basis, discarding a correct statement. Together, these traps push students toward option (a) — Statement 1 only — when the correct answer is (c) — Statements 1 and 3.
en.final_explanation:
British administrative coercion at Kheda followed a calculated but ultimately unsuccessful strategy. Understanding its logic and failure is key to understanding why Kheda became a template for later resistance movements.

• Statement 1 — Correct: The colonial administration targeted movable property — cattle, implements, crops — deliberately avoiding land seizure. The calculation was that movable property loss would be painful enough to force compliance without the political risk of dispossessing peasants of land, which could trigger a broader uprising.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: British coercion at Kheda failed. Peasants concealed cattle and implements before officials arrived; when auctions were held, neighboring peasants refused to bid, rendering confiscated items unsaleable. The strategy backfired.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The paradox of coercion-strengthening-solidarity is precisely documented at Kheda. When the British threatened everyone collectively, individual defection became socially stigmatizing — communities closed ranks. This pattern recurred at Bardoli (1928) and was an important lesson in satyagraha strategy.

Value Addition:
• Asset concealment and auction refusal became standard community counter-tactics in later revenue non-payment movements.
• The British preference for movable over immovable asset distraint reflects the colonial state's fear of agrarian rebellion — land dispossession risked transforming a limited fiscal dispute into an existential confrontation.
• The paradox of coercion strengthening solidarity has a modern social science analog in 'reactive collective identity' theory.

hi.display_text:
खेड़ा सत्याग्रह (1918) के प्रति ब्रिटिश प्रशासनिक प्रतिक्रिया के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

1. ब्रिटिश प्रशासन ने विशेष रूप से चल संपत्ति — मवेशी, कृषि उपकरण, और खड़ी फसल — को जब्ती और नीलामी के लिए निशाना बनाया, भूमि के खिलाफ सीधे कार्रवाई से जानबूझकर बचते हुए।
2. खेड़ा में ब्रिटिश दबावकारी उपाय अत्यंत प्रभावी साबित हुए, क्योंकि मवेशी की नीलामी की धमकी से अधिकांश पटिदार परिवारों ने पहले महीने के भीतर राजस्व भुगतान फिर से शुरू कर दिया।
3. खेड़ा में ब्रिटिश दबावकारी उपायों की विफलता ने एक ऐसा पैटर्न दिखाया जिसमें सामूहिक अवज्ञा का अभ्यास करने वाले समुदायों पर राज्य द्वारा लगाया गया दबाव विरोधाभासी रूप से एकजुटता को मजबूत करता है बजाय इसके कि वह अलगाव उत्पन्न करे।

उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?

(a) केवल 1
(b) केवल 2 और 3
(c) केवल 1 और 3
(d) 1, 2 और 3

statement_analysis.statement: खेड़ा सत्याग्रह के दौरान ब्रिटिश प्रशासन ने विशेष रूप से चल संपत्ति — मवेशी, कृषि उपकरण, और खड़ी फसल — को जब्ती और नीलामी के लिए निशाना बनाया, भूमि के खिलाफ सीधे कार्रवाई से जानबूझकर बचते हुए।
statement_analysis.reason: यह चयनात्मक जब्ती रणनीति एक जानबूझकर औपनिवेशिक गणना थी: भूमि पर हमला एक बड़ी और अधिक खतरनाक विद्रोह को जन्म देगा, जबकि चल संपत्ति को निशाना बनाना एक अनुपातिक दबाव प्रतिक्रिया प्रतीत होती थी जो संघर्ष को बढ़ाए बिना अनुपालन को मजबूर कर सकती थी।

statement_analysis.statement: खेड़ा में ब्रिटिश दबावकारी उपाय अत्यंत प्रभावी साबित हुए, क्योंकि मवेशी की नीलामी की धमकी से अधिकांश पटिदार परिवारों ने पहले महीने के भीतर राजस्व भुगतान फिर से शुरू कर दिया।
statement_analysis.reason: खेड़ा में ब्रिटिश दबावकारी उपाय अप्रभावी थे — किसान अधिकारियों के आने से पहले संपत्ति छुपा देते थे, और पड़ोसी नीलामी में बोली लगाने से इनकार कर देते थे, जिससे जब्ती रणनीति अप्रभावी हो गई। विरोधाभास यह है कि दबाव ने किसान एकजुटता को तोड़ने के बजाय मजबूत किया।

statement_analysis.statement: खेड़ा में ब्रिटिश दबावकारी उपायों की विफलता ने एक ऐसा पैटर्न दिखाया जिसमें सामूहिक अवज्ञा का अभ्यास करने वाले समुदायों पर राज्य द्वारा लगाया गया दबाव विरोधाभासी रूप से एकजुटता को मजबूत करता है बजाय इसके कि वह अलगाव उत्पन्न करे।
statement_analysis.reason: यह गतिशीलता — दबाव से सामूहिक कार्रवाई की मजबूती — खेड़ा में प्रलेखित है और बड़ौली (1928) तथा अन्य सत्याग्रहों में भी दोहराई गई। जब सभी सदस्य एक समान खतरे का सामना करते हैं, तो व्यक्तिगत अलगाव सामाजिक रूप से महंगा हो जाता है, जिससे सामूहिक प्रतिरोध बना रहता है।

hi.strong_distractor: d — विकल्प (d) भ्रामक है क्योंकि कथन 3 की शैक्षणिक-शब्दावली 'विरोधाभासी एकजुटता की मजबूती' छात्रों को अतिव्याख्या लग सकती है, जिससे वे इसे अस्वीकार कर केवल कथन 1 को सही मानकर विकल्प (a) चुन सकते हैं।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 सत्यापित करें: चल संपत्ति को लक्षित कर भूमि जब्ती से बचना खेड़ा में ब्रिटिश रणनीति के रूप में ऐतिहासिक रूप से प्रलेखित है — सही।
कथन 2 सत्यापित करें: खेड़ा में ब्रिटिश दबाव प्रभावी नहीं था — नीलामी विफल रही क्योंकि संपत्ति छुपाई गई और पड़ोसी एकजुट थे। 'अधिकांश ने भुगतान फिर से शुरू किया' दावा गलत है — इसे गलत चिह्नित करें।
कथन 3 सत्यापित करें: दबाव से एकजुटता की मजबूती की गतिशीलता खेड़ा में प्रलेखित है और समान आंदोलनों के व्यापक ऐतिहासिक रिकॉर्ड के अनुरूप है। कथन 3 सही है।
कथन 1 और 3 सही हैं — विकल्प (c)।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 2 सीधे तौर पर खेड़ा में हुई वास्तविकता के विपरीत है — ब्रिटिश दबाव पूरी तरह विफल रहा, एकजुटता को तोड़ने के बजाय मजबूत किया। जो छात्र याद करते हैं कि ब्रिटिश ने दबाव डाला था, वे शायद याद न रख पाएं कि वह सफल रहा या नहीं, और कथन 2 की आत्मविश्वासी भाषा ('अधिकांश ने पहले महीने में भुगतान फिर से शुरू किया') विश्वसनीय लगती है। कथन 3 की शैक्षणिक अभिव्यक्ति छात्रों को इसके तथ्यात्मक आधार पर संदेह करने पर मजबूर कर सकती है, जिससे वे सही कथन को खारिज कर देते हैं। ये जाल छात्र को विकल्प (a) — केवल कथन 1 — की ओर ले जाते हैं, जबकि सही उत्तर (c) — कथन 1 और 3 है।
hi.final_explanation:
खेड़ा में ब्रिटिश प्रशासनिक दबाव एक सोची-समझी लेकिन अंततः असफल रणनीति थी। इसकी तर्क और विफलता को समझना यह समझने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है कि क्यों खेड़ा बाद के प्रतिरोध आंदोलनों के लिए एक मॉडल बन गया।

• कथन 1 — सही: औपनिवेशिक प्रशासन ने चल संपत्ति — मवेशी, उपकरण, फसल — को निशाना बनाया, भूमि जब्ती से जानबूझकर बचा। गणना यह थी कि चल संपत्ति का नुकसान इतना कष्टदायक होगा कि वह अनुपालन को मजबूर करेगा बिना किसानों की भूमि छीनने के राजनीतिक जोखिम के, जो व्यापक विद्रोह को जन्म दे सकता था।
• कथन 2 — गलत: खेड़ा में ब्रिटिश दबाव विफल रहा। किसान अधिकारियों के आने से पहले मवेशी और उपकरण छुपा देते थे; जब नीलामी हुई, तो पड़ोसी किसानों ने बोली लगाने से इनकार कर दिया, जिससे जब्त वस्तुएं बेची नहीं जा सकीं। यह रणनीति उल्टी पड़ गई।
• कथन 3 — सही: दबाव से एकजुटता की मजबूती का विरोधाभास ठीक उसी तरह खेड़ा में प्रलेखित है। जब ब्रिटिश ने सभी को सामूहिक रूप से धमकाया, तो व्यक्तिगत अलगाव सामाजिक रूप से कलंकित हो गया — समुदाय ने एकजुटता बनाए रखी। यह पैटर्न बड़ौली (1928) में भी दोहराया गया और सत्याग्रह रणनीति में एक महत्वपूर्ण सबक था।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• संपत्ति छुपाना और नीलामी में बोली न लगाना बाद के राजस्व अवैतनिक आंदोलनों में सामान्य सामुदायिक प्रतिकार रणनीतियाँ बन गईं।
• चल संपत्ति को जब्त करने की ब्रिटिश प्राथमिकता औपनिवेशिक राज्य के कृषि विद्रोह के भय को दर्शाती है — भूमि छीनना एक सीमित वित्तीय विवाद को अस्तित्वगत टकराव में बदल सकता था।
• दबाव से एकजुटता की मजबूती का विरोधाभास आधुनिक सामाजिक विज्ञान में 'प्रतिक्रियाशील सामूहिक पहचान' सिद्धांत के अनुरूप है।

table_data.header_text: Match the following Gandhi-led campaigns with the primary communication/media strategy that distinguished each:
rows: A. Champaran Satyagraha (1917)
1. Systematic collection of peasant testimony for presentation before a formal inquiry commission
B. Kheda Satyagraha (1918)
2. Vernacular press in Gujarati (Navajivan) for rural peasant mobilization alongside English press for educated audiences
C. Salt Satyagraha / Dandi March (1930)
3. Mass meeting networks and boycott announcements through Congress organizational structures
D. Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22)
4. Orchestrated media events designed for maximum visual impact and international press coverage
table_data.footer_text:
Which of the following is the correct matching?

(a) A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3
(b) A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3
(c) A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4
(d) A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3

en.strong_distractor: a — Option (a) is deceptive because it correctly pairs Kheda with vernacular press (Navajivan) but wrongly pairs Champaran with 'active media campaigning,' when Champaran's distinctive method was systematic inquiry-based evidence-gathering and testimony collection — not media campaigning.
elimination_logic: Identify the unambiguous pair: Kheda — vernacular press (Navajivan) for rural Gujarati mobilization is firmly documented. Match B with 2.

Test Champaran's method: Champaran relied on Gandhi systematically collecting peasant testimony and presenting evidence to a formal inquiry commission — inquiry-based reporting, not active media campaigning. Match A with 1.
Salt Satyagraha (1930) involved orchestrated media events (the Dandi march itself was staged for maximum press coverage, with journalists invited) — match C with 4.
Non-Cooperation Movement used mass meeting networks and boycott announcements more than any single media tool — match D with 3. This gives option (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap centers on conflating Champaran's inquiry-reporting method with Kheda's active media campaigning. Both involved publicizing peasant grievances, making them seem similar at the surface. The precise distinction — Champaran used evidence collection for a formal inquiry (passive evidence presentation) while Kheda used active newspaper campaigning (proactive public mobilization) — requires careful knowledge of each movement's specific media strategy. Option (a) exploits this by swapping the two methods between Champaran and Kheda.
en.final_explanation:
Each major Gandhi-led campaign had a distinct media and communication strategy suited to its specific method and audience.

Correct pairings:
• A (Champaran, 1917) — 1 (Systematic collection of peasant testimony for formal inquiry commission): Champaran's media method was evidence-based — Gandhi gathered testimony to present before the Champaran Inquiry Commission, using documentation rather than newspaper campaigning.
• B (Kheda Satyagraha, 1918) — 2 (Vernacular press — Navajivan in Gujarati — for rural peasant mobilization): Kheda pioneered the use of Gujarati-language Navajivan to reach a rural, semi-literate peasant audience alongside the English Young India for educated readers.
• C (Salt Satyagraha, 1930) — 4 (Orchestrated media events designed for maximum visual impact and international press coverage): The Dandi March was deliberately staged as a 24-day media spectacle — journalists were invited, each day's march was reported, and the final act of picking up salt was a globally telegraphed image.
• D (Non-Cooperation Movement, 1920–22) — 3 (Mass meeting networks and boycott announcements across Congress organizational structures): Non-Cooperation relied on mass meeting mobilization — Congress organizational networks rather than a single media tool.

Value Addition:
• The evolution from Champaran's inquiry-reporting (1917) to Kheda's active campaigning (1918) to Salt March's orchestrated media spectacle (1930) maps Gandhi's growing media sophistication.
• International press coverage became a deliberate strategic asset only from the Salt March onward.
• Navajivan (Gujarati) reached the peasant base; Young India (English) reached the international audience — a dual-track approach innovated at Kheda.

• C (नमक सत्याग्रह / डांडी मार्च, 1930) — 4 (अधिकतम दृश्य प्रभाव और अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रेस कवरेज के लिए योजनाबद्ध मीडिया कार्यक्रम): डांडी मार्च जानबूझकर 24-दिन का मीडिया तमाशा था — पत्रकारों को आमंत्रित किया गया, प्रत्येक दिन की मार्च की रिपोर्टिंग हुई, और नमक उठाने का अंतिम कृत्य विश्वव्यापी टेलीग्राफिक छवि था।

meta.subject: Modern History
concepts_used: Legacy of Kheda Satyagraha in Post-Independence Revenue and Land Policies
Limitations and Critiques of Kheda Satyagraha

shared.concept_anchor: Rightful resistance state rules against state Kheda legacy

en.display_text:
In a contemporary district of Gujarat, a group of farmers whose crops have been severely damaged by unseasonal flooding approach the district revenue officer demanding relief from land revenue assessment for that agricultural year. They cite a provision in the state's Land Revenue Code that specifies revenue suspension when crop yield falls below a prescribed statutory threshold. The officer refuses, arguing that official crop surveys show yield above the threshold, while farmers present their own village-level documentation showing severe damage. The farmers organize a collective public petition citing only the state's own statutory provision — making no demand beyond what the law already provides.

Which of the following principles does this scenario most directly exemplify, and what is its historical antecedent in India's freedom movement?

(a) Civil disobedience through non-payment — pioneered at Kheda (1918) where peasants refused revenue payment as a moral act of non-cooperation
(b) Extra-constitutional pressure through mass mobilization — reflecting the Non-Cooperation Movement's method of overwhelming administrative machinery
(c) Rightful resistance — using the state's own legal framework against its arbitrary non-application, reflecting the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) precedent of invoking colonial revenue rules against the colonial administration's refusal to apply them
(d) Zamindari abolition precedent — reflecting post-independence land reforms that established peasants' rights against arbitrary state extraction from landed intermediaries
en.strong_distractor: a — Option (a) is deceptive because 'civil disobedience through non-payment' describes the method used at Kheda accurately, but the question asks which principle explains peasants using the state's own statutory thresholds — a different, more precise concept than generic civil disobedience.
elimination_logic: The scenario describes peasants invoking a statutory crop damage threshold from a post-independence land revenue code to demand relief — the key feature is using the state's own legal standard against the state's arbitrary refusal.

Eliminate option (a): 'Civil disobedience through non-payment' describes the Kheda method, not the principle being applied in the scenario — the scenario's farmers are not refusing to pay, they are demanding compliance with an existing rule.

Eliminate option (b): 'Extra-constitutional pressure through mass mobilization' describes Non-Cooperation/Civil Disobedience movements — the scenario farmers are working within the legal framework, not outside it.
Eliminate option (d): 'Zamindari abolition precedent' addresses land tenure systems, not revenue relief during crop failure — irrelevant to this scenario.

Confirm option (c): 'Rightful resistance — using the state's own legal framework against its arbitrary non-application' is precisely what both the scenario farmers and the Kheda peasants of 1918 were doing.
en.final_explanation:
The Kheda Satyagraha established a template of 'rightful resistance' — peasants using the colonial state's own administrative rules to demand compliance, rather than challenging the revenue system's legitimacy. This template influenced post-independence land revenue law and peasant political culture in Gujarat.

The scenario presents farmers invoking a statutory provision in a state Land Revenue Code (a direct post-independence codification of the Kheda principle) to demand relief from a rigid administrative refusal. The principle at work is not civil disobedience (the farmers are working within the legal system) or extra-constitutional pressure (they are citing law, not defying it).

• Option (a) — Civil disobedience through non-payment: Incorrect. The scenario farmers are making a legal claim, not refusing payment — civil disobedience involves deliberate law-breaking as a moral statement.
• Option (b) — Extra-constitutional mass mobilization: Incorrect. The farmers are using statutory provisions, not going outside the constitutional framework.
• Option (c) — Rightful resistance: Correct. Farmers citing the state's own statutory threshold against the state's refusal to apply it is precisely the 'rightful resistance' framework — using the state's rules as a weapon against its arbitrary application.
• Option (d) — Zamindari abolition precedent: Incorrect. Zamindari abolition addressed land tenure and landlord-tenant relations, not government revenue assessment during crop failure.

Value Addition:
• The codification of crop-failure revenue relief in post-independence Land Revenue Codes is a direct institutional legacy of Kheda.
• 'Rightful resistance' as an academic concept examines how subordinate groups use the dominant group's own norms against arbitrary power.
• This principle distinguishes Kheda from revolutionary peasant movements — it worked within, not against, the existing legal order.

hi.display_text:
गुजरात के एक समकालीन जिले में, एक समूह किसान जिनकी फसलें असामयिक बाढ़ से गंभीर रूप से क्षतिग्रस्त हुई हैं, जिला राजस्व अधिकारी के पास उस कृषि वर्ष के लिए भूमि राजस्व आकलन से राहत की मांग करते हुए आते हैं। वे राज्य के भूमि राजस्व संहिता के एक प्रावधान का हवाला देते हैं जो निर्धारित वैधानिक मानदंड से नीचे फसल उत्पादन होने पर राजस्व निलंबन निर्दिष्ट करता है। अधिकारी इनकार करता है, तर्क देते हुए कि आधिकारिक फसल सर्वेक्षण मानदंड से ऊपर उत्पादन दिखाते हैं, जबकि किसान अपने गांव स्तर के दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत करते हैं जो गंभीर क्षति दिखाते हैं। किसान केवल राज्य के अपने वैधानिक प्रावधान का हवाला देते हुए एक सामूहिक सार्वजनिक याचिका आयोजित करते हैं — वे कानून से परे कोई मांग नहीं करते।

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सिद्धांत इस परिदृश्य का सबसे प्रत्यक्ष उदाहरण है, और इसका भारत के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में क्या ऐतिहासिक पूर्ववर्ती है?

(a) गैर-भुगतान के माध्यम से सविनय अवज्ञा — खेडा (1918) में अग्रणी, जहां किसानों ने राजस्व भुगतान को नैतिक असहयोग के रूप में ठुकरा दिया था
(b) जन आंदोलन के माध्यम से असंवैधानिक दबाव — असहयोग आंदोलन की प्रशासनिक मशीनरी को अभिभूत करने की विधि को दर्शाता है
(c) सही प्रतिरोध — राज्य के अपने कानूनी ढांचे का मनमानी अनुप्रयोग के खिलाफ उपयोग, खेडा सत्याग्रह (1918) के औपनिवेशिक राजस्व नियमों को प्रशासन के अस्वीकृति के खिलाफ लागू करने के उदाहरण को दर्शाता है
(d) जमींदारी उन्मूलन का उदाहरण — स्वतंत्रता के बाद की भूमि सुधारों को दर्शाता है जिसने किसानों के अधिकारों को जमींदारों से मनमानी राज्य निकासी के खिलाफ स्थापित किया
hi.strong_distractor: a — विकल्प (a) भ्रामक है क्योंकि 'गैर-भुगतान के माध्यम से सविनय अवज्ञा' खेडा में प्रयुक्त विधि का सही वर्णन करता है, लेकिन प्रश्न यह पूछता है कि कौन-सा सिद्धांत किसानों द्वारा राज्य के अपने वैधानिक मानदंडों का उपयोग करने को समझाता है — जो सामान्य सविनय अवज्ञा से अलग, अधिक सटीक अवधारणा है।
elimination_logic: यह परिदृश्य किसानों द्वारा स्वतंत्रता के बाद के भूमि राजस्व संहिता के एक वैधानिक फसल क्षति मानदंड का हवाला देकर राहत मांगने का वर्णन करता है — मुख्य विशेषता यह है कि वे राज्य के अपने कानूनी मानक का राज्य की मनमानी अस्वीकृति के खिलाफ उपयोग कर रहे हैं।

विकल्प (a) को निरस्त करें: 'गैर-भुगतान के माध्यम से सविनय अवज्ञा' खेडा की विधि का वर्णन करता है, पर परिदृश्य में प्रयुक्त सिद्धांत का नहीं — परिदृश्य के किसान भुगतान से इनकार नहीं कर रहे, वे मौजूदा नियम के अनुपालन की मांग कर रहे हैं।
विकल्प (b) को निरस्त करें: 'जन आंदोलन के माध्यम से असंवैधानिक दबाव' असहयोग/सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलनों का वर्णन करता है — परिदृश्य के किसान कानूनी ढांचे के भीतर काम कर रहे हैं, बाहर नहीं।
विकल्प (d) को निरस्त करें: 'जमींदारी उन्मूलन का उदाहरण' भूमि स्वामित्व प्रणालियों से संबंधित है, फसल विफलता के दौरान राजस्व राहत से नहीं — यह परिदृश्य से अप्रासंगिक है।
विकल्प (c) की पुष्टि करें: 'सही प्रतिरोध — राज्य के अपने कानूनी ढांचे का मनमानी अनुप्रयोग के खिलाफ उपयोग' बिल्कुल वही है जो परिदृश्य के किसान और 1918 के खेडा के किसान कर रहे थे।
hi.final_explanation:
खेडा सत्याग्रह ने 'सही प्रतिरोध' का एक प्रारूप स्थापित किया — किसानों द्वारा औपनिवेशिक राज्य के अपने प्रशासनिक नियमों का उपयोग कर अनुपालन की मांग करना, न कि राजस्व प्रणाली की वैधता को चुनौती देना। इस प्रारूप ने स्वतंत्रता के बाद गुजरात में भूमि राजस्व कानून और किसान राजनीतिक संस्कृति को प्रभावित किया।

यह परिदृश्य किसानों द्वारा राज्य के भूमि राजस्व संहिता के एक वैधानिक प्रावधान का हवाला देते हुए कठोर प्रशासनिक अस्वीकृति के खिलाफ राहत मांगने का उदाहरण प्रस्तुत करता है। यहां प्रयुक्त सिद्धांत सविनय अवज्ञा नहीं है (किसान कानूनी प्रणाली के भीतर काम कर रहे हैं) और न ही असंवैधानिक दबाव (वे कानून का हवाला दे रहे हैं, उसका उल्लंघन नहीं)।

• विकल्प (a) — गैर-भुगतान के माध्यम से सविनय अवज्ञा: गलत। परिदृश्य के किसान कानूनी दावा कर रहे हैं, भुगतान से इनकार नहीं कर रहे — सविनय अवज्ञा जानबूझकर कानून तोड़ने का नैतिक बयान है।
• विकल्प (b) — असंवैधानिक जन आंदोलन: गलत। किसान वैधानिक प्रावधानों का उपयोग कर रहे हैं, संवैधानिक ढांचे के बाहर नहीं जा रहे।
• विकल्प (c) — सही प्रतिरोध: सही। किसान राज्य के अपने वैधानिक मानदंड का राज्य की मनमानी अनुप्रयोग के खिलाफ उपयोग कर रहे हैं, जो 'सही प्रतिरोध' का सटीक उदाहरण है।
• विकल्प (d) — जमींदारी उन्मूलन का उदाहरण: गलत। जमींदारी उन्मूलन भूमि स्वामित्व और जमींदार-किसान संबंधों से संबंधित था, फसल विफलता के दौरान सरकारी राजस्व आकलन से नहीं।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• स्वतंत्रता के बाद के भूमि राजस्व संहिताओं में फसल विफलता पर राजस्व राहत का संहिताकरण खेडा का प्रत्यक्ष संस्थागत विरासत है।
• 'सही प्रतिरोध' एक शैक्षणिक अवधारणा है जो अधीनस्थ समूहों द्वारा प्रभुत्व समूह के अपने नियमों का मनमानी शक्ति के खिलाफ उपयोग की व्याख्या करती है।
• यह सिद्धांत खेडा को क्रांतिकारी किसान आंदोलनों से अलग करता है — यह मौजूदा कानूनी व्यवस्था के भीतर काम करता था, उसके खिलाफ नहीं।

en.display_text:
With reference to the concept of 'moral victory' as applied to the Kheda Satyagraha (1918), consider the following statements:

1. Gandhi's declaration of the Kheda Satyagraha as a 'moral victory' was strategically important for sustaining subsequent movements by preventing demoralization after an inconclusive settlement.
2. Historians who critique Gandhi's 'moral victory' declaration at Kheda argue that routinely declaring ambiguous outcomes as victories ultimately strengthened the credibility of satyagraha as a political method by demonstrating its principled consistency.
3. The philosophical basis of the 'moral victory' concept — that satyagraha aims at the adversary's inner transformation, not just material concession — is a genuine element of Gandhian political theory, even if its application at Kheda has been contested.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Gandhi's declaration of the Kheda Satyagraha as a 'moral victory' was strategically important for sustaining subsequent movements by preventing demoralization after an inconclusive settlement.
statement_analysis.reason: The 'moral victory' framing served a specific strategic function — maintaining the psychological momentum of the satyagraha method among participants and observers, even when the material outcome was ambiguous. This framing was subsequently used in other inconclusive satyagraha outcomes.

statement_analysis.statement: Historians who critique Gandhi's 'moral victory' declaration at Kheda argue that routinely declaring ambiguous outcomes as victories ultimately strengthened the credibility of satyagraha as a political method by demonstrating its principled consistency.
statement_analysis.reason: The historiographical critique argues the opposite — that declaring ambiguous outcomes as victories risks eroding credibility by blurring the line between genuine success and face-saving rationalization, not strengthening credibility.

statement_analysis.statement: The philosophical basis of the 'moral victory' concept — that satyagraha aims at the adversary's inner transformation, not just material concession — is a genuine element of Gandhian political theory, even if its application at Kheda has been contested.
statement_analysis.reason: Gandhi's satyagraha philosophy genuinely held that the transformation of the adversary's conscience was the ultimate goal — this is documented in his writings. The contestation at Kheda is about whether this principle was correctly applied to an ambiguous outcome, not whether the principle itself exists.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option (d) — all three — is deceptive because Statement 3's philosophical claim sounds authoritative and both Statements 1 and 3 are correct, leading students who accept all three to select option (d).
elimination_logic: Verify Statement 1: The 'moral victory' declaration's strategic function in preventing movement demoralization is historically documented and analytically sound — correct.
Verify Statement 2: The critique from historians is that ambiguous victory declarations erode credibility, not strengthen it — Statement 2 reverses the critique. Mark incorrect.
Verify Statement 3: Gandhi's satyagraha theory does include the adversary's inner transformation as a goal — this is well-documented in his writings and writings about him. Mark correct.
Statements 1 and 3 correct, Statement 2 incorrect — option (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 uses reversed-causation: it takes the real historiographical critique (ambiguous victory declarations erode credibility) and states the exact opposite (they strengthen credibility) in a confident, plausible-sounding way. Students who know the debate exists but haven't internalized the direction of the critique will accept Statement 2 as 'approximately what historians say' without catching the reversal. The presence of two clearly correct statements (1 and 3) creates pressure to include Statement 2 to reach 'all three,' which is option (d) — the trap.
en.final_explanation:
The 'moral victory' concept is one of the most philosophically rich and historiographically contested elements of Gandhian satyagraha theory.

• Statement 1 — Correct: The strategic value of the 'moral victory' framing was real — it prevented participant demoralization, maintained the credibility of the satyagraha method in organizers' eyes, and created a template for interpreting other inconclusive outcomes. Without such framing, a series of ambiguous outcomes could have destroyed the movement's momentum.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: This reverses the historians' actual critique. Scholars who question the 'moral victory' declaration argue it risks eroding credibility — if any outcome can be declared a victory, the concept of victory becomes meaningless, undermining the movement's moral authority over time.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Gandhi's philosophical framework genuinely included adversary transformation as the ultimate satyagraha goal. This is documented in 'Hind Swaraj' and other Gandhi writings. The debate about Kheda is not whether this principle exists, but whether an informal government concession constitutes 'adversary transformation.'

Value Addition:
• The 'moral victory' concept is strategically important because it reframes the measure of success — from material concession to moral impact.
• Bardoli (1928) did not require a 'moral victory' framing — it had a concrete formal outcome.
• Historians' debate about Kheda's outcome is part of the broader debate about whether Gandhian satyagraha delivered material results or primarily moral capital.

खेड़ा सत्याग्रह (1918) में लागू 'नैतिक विजय' की अवधारणा के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?

(a) केवल 1
(b) केवल 1 और 3
(c) केवल 2 और 3
(d) 1, 2 और 3

'नैतिक विजय' अवधारणा गांधीवादी सत्याग्रह सिद्धांत के सबसे दार्शनिक रूप से समृद्ध और इतिहासकारों द्वारा विवादित तत्वों में से एक है।

• कथन 1 — सही: 'नैतिक विजय' की व्याख्या का रणनीतिक महत्व वास्तविक था — इसने प्रतिभागियों के हतोत्साहन को रोका, आयोजकों की दृष्टि में सत्याग्रह पद्धति की विश्वसनीयता बनाए रखी, और अन्य अनिर्णायक परिणामों की व्याख्या के लिए एक ढांचा बनाया। बिना ऐसी व्याख्या के, अस्पष्ट परिणामों की श्रृंखला आंदोलन की गति को नष्ट कर सकती थी।
• कथन 2 — गलत: यह इतिहासकारों की वास्तविक आलोचना को उलट देता है। जो विद्वान 'नैतिक विजय' घोषणा पर सवाल उठाते हैं, वे तर्क देते हैं कि यदि कोई भी परिणाम विजय घोषित किया जा सकता है, तो विजय की अवधारणा निरर्थक हो जाती है, जिससे आंदोलन की नैतिक प्राधिकरण समय के साथ कमजोर होती है।
• कथन 3 — सही: गांधी का दार्शनिक ढांचा वास्तव में विरोधी के आंतरिक परिवर्तन को अंतिम सत्याग्रह लक्ष्य के रूप में शामिल करता है। यह 'हिंद स्वराज' और अन्य गांधी लेखों में प्रलेखित है। खेड़ा के बारे में बहस इस बात की नहीं है कि यह सिद्धांत मौजूद है या नहीं, बल्कि यह है कि क्या एक अनौपचारिक सरकारी रियायत को 'विरोधी का परिवर्तन' माना जा सकता है।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• 'नैतिक विजय' अवधारणा रणनीतिक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह सफलता के माप को पुनः परिभाषित करती है — भौतिक रियायत से नैतिक प्रभाव तक।
• बारदोली (1928) को 'नैतिक विजय' की व्याख्या की आवश्यकता नहीं थी — उसका एक ठोस औपचारिक परिणाम था।
• खेड़ा के परिणाम पर इतिहासकारों की बहस व्यापक बहस का हिस्सा है कि क्या गांधीवादी सत्याग्रह ने भौतिक परिणाम दिए या मुख्यतः नैतिक पूंजी।

इंदुलाल याग्निक UPSC के लिए 'खेड़ा के बाद क्या हुआ' के महत्वपूर्ण पहलू का प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं। वे खेड़ा सत्याग्रह के किसान आंदोलन में वास्तविक प्रतिभागी थे, लेकिन उनका बाद का राजनीतिक करियर गांधीवादी मुख्यधारा का अनुसरण नहीं करता था।

• विकल्प (b) — गलत: शंकरलाल बैंकर की भूमिका शहरी कांग्रेस नेटवर्क और ग्रामीण खेड़ा किसानों के बीच संगठनात्मक कनेक्टर की थी — उन्हें खेड़ा याचिका का लेखक बताना संस्था-गुण स्वैप है।

• विकल्प (d) — गलत: बड़ौली सत्याग्रह पटेल के नेतृत्व में था, याग्निक का नहीं। याग्निक का बाद का करियर गुजरात कांग्रेस मुख्यधारा से अलग था।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• कम ज्ञात खेड़ा हस्तियों — याग्निक, बैंकर — को विशेष रूप से रटने वाले और विश्लेषणात्मक ज्ञान के बीच अंतर करने के लिए परखा जाता है।
• खेड़ा से बड़ौली का मार्ग पटेल के कार्यकर्ताओं ने अपनाया, याग्निक ने नहीं, जो खेड़ा प्रतिभागियों के बाद के रास्तों की आंतरिक विविधता को दर्शाता है।
• गुजरात की स्वतंत्रता के बाद की राजनीतिक विविधता (कांग्रेस, समाजवादी, दलित आंदोलन) आंशिक रूप से खेड़ा युग के कार्यकर्ताओं के अलग-अलग मार्गों से जुड़ी है।

statement_analysis.statement: Kheda (1918), Bardoli (1928), and the Dandi Salt March (1930) are all Gujarat-based campaigns with an organizational continuity — trained workers from each earlier campaign contributed to the subsequent one.
statement_analysis.reason: Institutional continuity across Gujarat's three major campaigns is historically documented — Kheda-trained workers contributed to Bardoli's organization, and Bardoli veterans participated in the Dandi preparations. statement_analysis.statement: The Dandi Salt March (1930) was structurally similar to the Kheda Satyagraha in that both were local, district-level campaigns targeting a single specific colonial revenue or taxation policy.
statement_analysis.reason: The Dandi Salt March was a national campaign — not a local or district-level movement. While it began in Gujarat and targeted the salt tax (a specific policy), it was designed and functioned as an all-India catalyst for mass civil disobedience, unlike Kheda's explicitly regional character.

statement_analysis.statement: Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) achieved a clearer formal outcome than Kheda (1918) — the government appointed an inquiry committee whose findings favored the peasants, unlike Kheda's informal unwritten settlement.
statement_analysis.reason: The Broomfield-Maxwell inquiry committee appointed after Bardoli examined the revenue enhancement and found it unjustified, leading to a formal government concession — a substantially more concrete outcome than Kheda's informal oral instruction to revenue collectors.

statement_analysis.statement: The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was the first instance in which Gandhi employed a complete mass non-cooperation strategy at the national level, making it the direct precursor to the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22).
statement_analysis.reason: Kheda was explicitly regional — confined to Kheda district in Gujarat — not national in scope. The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920) was Gandhi's first national-scale mass civil disobedience. Describing Kheda as 'national level' contradicts its documented geographic limitation.

en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2's trap is attributing 'local, district-level' character to the Dandi Salt March — a movement that began locally but was deliberately designed for national and international impact. Students who associate Dandi with Gujarat (the starting point) may accept 'local' without questioning whether the march's scope was regional or national. Statement 4 correctly identifies Kheda as a precursor but falsely attributes 'national level' to it — students who know Kheda influenced later national movements may accept 'national level' as a reasonable characterization of its importance rather than its geographic scope.
en.final_explanation:
Gujarat's three major campaigns — Kheda (1918), Bardoli (1928), Dandi (1930) — have a complex relationship of similarity, continuity, and difference.

| Statement | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Organizational continuity Kheda-Bardoli-Dandi | Correct |
| Dandi as 'local district-level' like Kheda | Incorrect |
| Bardoli's formal inquiry vs. Kheda's informal settlement | Correct |
| Kheda as 'first national level non-cooperation' | Incorrect |

• Statement 1 — Correct: Cadre continuity is documented — Kheda workers → Bardoli; Bardoli veterans → Dandi preparations.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: The Dandi Salt March was national in design and impact. It began in Gujarat but was intended (and functioned) as an all-India catalyst — fundamentally different from Kheda's district-confined character.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Bardoli's outcome was formally documented through inquiry; Kheda's was an informal oral instruction — clearer Bardoli victory.
• Statement 4 — Incorrect: Kheda was regional, not national. The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920) was Gandhi's first national-scale campaign.

• Dandi's national impact was achieved through deliberate media orchestration — journalists were invited for maximum coverage.
• The Kheda-Bardoli-Dandi continuity makes Gujarat the state with the densest organizational legacy from the freedom struggle.
• 'Local laboratory → national application' is the precise Kheda-to-Non-Cooperation transition Gandhi described.

en.display_text:
The Kheda Satyagraha of 1918 was distinguished from other peasant movements of the period by the specific nature of its central grievance. Which of the following accurately identifies that grievance?

(a) Opposition to forced indigo cultivation imposed by European planters on peasants of Kheda district under contractual obligations
(b) Resistance to insecure land tenure arrangements and arbitrary evictions by zamindars in the Kheda region of Gujarat
(c) Refusal to pay colonial government land revenue demands during a period of crop failure, on the grounds that the yield had fallen below the legally prescribed remission threshold
(d) Protest against excessive irrigation water charges levied by the colonial administration on cultivators in the Kheda district
en.strong_distractor: a — Option (a) is deceptive because 'peasant movement' and 'Gujarat' together in the option sound correct, and students unfamiliar with the precise distinction between Kheda's and Champaran's issues may accept 'indigo cultivation' as a generic 'Gujarat peasant grievance.'
elimination_logic: Eliminate option (a): Forced indigo cultivation was the Champaran (Bihar) grievance, not a Kheda issue — geographic-swap and conflation.
Eliminate option (b): Land tenure and zamindari disputes were associated with other agrarian movements (Bengal, UP) — not the specific Kheda issue.
Eliminate option (d): Excessive irrigation water charges were an agrarian grievance elsewhere (e.g., Deccan riots) but not identified as Kheda's central dispute.

Confirm option (c): Kheda's dispute was precisely and exclusively about the colonial government's demand for land revenue during a period of crop failure — a fiscal/administrative grievance against the colonial state.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Option (a) exploits the Champaran-Kheda conflation — both are Gandhi's early Indian campaigns, both involve 'peasant distress,' and students who haven't internalized the distinction in the nature of grievances will accept 'forced indigo cultivation' as a plausible Gujarat peasant issue. The geographic-swap is reinforced by the general association of 'Gandhi's first Indian campaigns' without distinguishing their precise issues.
en.final_explanation:
The Kheda Satyagraha's central grievance is frequently misidentified — this is among the most tested basic facts about the movement.

• Option (a) — Incorrect: Forced indigo cultivation under the tinkathia system was Champaran's (Bihar) grievance against private European planters. Kheda had no indigo or planter involvement.
• Option (b) — Incorrect: Land tenure disputes (zamindari rights, security of tenure) were the grievance in other parts of India — Bengal's peasant movements, for instance. Kheda's issue was fiscal, not tenurial.
• Option (c) — Correct: Kheda's central and exclusive grievance was the colonial government's insistence on collecting full land revenue despite crop failure. Peasants argued their yield had fallen below the one-fourth threshold that legally entitled them to remission. This was a fiscal-administrative dispute with the colonial state directly.
• Option (d) — Incorrect: Irrigation water charges were an issue in Deccan and other contexts — not the Kheda dispute.

Value Addition:
• The distinction 'revenue dispute (Kheda) vs. agrarian contract dispute (Champaran)' is the single most important Kheda fact to retain.
• Kheda's grievance was also specifically NOT about abolishing land revenue — it was about applying the existing remission rule correctly.
• This fiscal precision made Kheda's demand legally defensible — a key reason Gandhi joined the campaign.

hi.display_text:
1918 के खेड़ा सत्याग्रह को उस अवधि के अन्य किसान आंदोलनों से उसके केंद्रीय शिकायत की विशिष्ट प्रकृति द्वारा अलग पहचाना गया। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा उस शिकायत की सही पहचान करता है?

(a) यूरोपीय प्लांटरों द्वारा खेड़ा जिले के किसानों पर अनुबंधात्मक बाध्यताओं के तहत जबरन इंडिगो की खेती का विरोध
(b) गुजरात के खेड़ा क्षेत्र में ज़मींदारों द्वारा असुरक्षित भूमि अधिकार व्यवस्था और मनमाने निकाले जाने का प्रतिरोध
(c) फसल खराबी के दौरान औपनिवेशिक सरकार की भूमि राजस्व मांगों का भुगतान करने से इनकार, इस आधार पर कि उपज कानूनी रूप से निर्धारित छूट सीमा से नीचे गिर गई थी
(d) खेड़ा जिले के कृषकों पर औपनिवेशिक प्रशासन द्वारा लगाए गए अत्यधिक सिंचाई जल शुल्क के खिलाफ विरोध
hi.strong_distractor: a — विकल्प (a) धोखाधड़ीपूर्ण है क्योंकि 'किसान आंदोलन' और 'गुजरात' एक साथ विकल्प में सही लगते हैं, और जो छात्र खेड़ा और चंपारण की समस्याओं के बीच सटीक अंतर से परिचित नहीं हैं वे 'इंडिगो की खेती' को सामान्य 'गुजरात किसान शिकायत' के रूप में स्वीकार कर सकते हैं।
elimination_logic: विकल्प (a) को निरस्त करें — जबरन इंडिगो की खेती चंपारण (बिहार) की शिकायत थी, खेड़ा का मुद्दा नहीं — भौगोलिक भ्रम और मिश्रण।
विकल्प (b) को निरस्त करें — ज़मीन के अधिकार और ज़मींदारी विवाद अन्य कृषि आंदोलनों (बंगाल, यूपी) से जुड़े थे — खेड़ा का विशिष्ट मुद्दा नहीं।

विकल्प (c) को पुष्टि करें — खेड़ा का विवाद सटीक और विशेष रूप से फसल खराबी के दौरान औपनिवेशिक सरकार की भूमि राजस्व मांग के बारे में था — औपनिवेशिक राज्य के खिलाफ वित्तीय/प्रशासनिक शिकायत।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: विकल्प (a) चंपारण-खेड़ा मिश्रण का शोषण करता है — दोनों गांधी के प्रारंभिक भारतीय अभियान हैं, दोनों में 'किसान कष्ट' शामिल है, और जो छात्र शिकायतों की प्रकृति में अंतर को नहीं समझते वे 'जबरन इंडिगो की खेती' को गुजरात किसान मुद्दे के रूप में स्वीकार कर लेते हैं। भौगोलिक भ्रम इस सामान्य संघ से मजबूत होता है कि 'गांधी के पहले भारतीय अभियान' बिना उनके सटीक मुद्दों के भेद के।
hi.final_explanation:
खेड़ा सत्याग्रह की केंद्रीय शिकायत अक्सर गलत पहचानी जाती है — यह आंदोलन के सबसे परीक्षण किए गए मूल तथ्यों में से एक है।

• विकल्प (a) — गलत: टिनकाठिया प्रणाली के तहत जबरन इंडिगो की खेती चंपारण (बिहार) की शिकायत थी जो निजी यूरोपीय प्लांटरों के खिलाफ थी। खेड़ा में इंडिगो या प्लांटरों की कोई भागीदारी नहीं थी।
• विकल्प (b) — गलत: ज़मीन के अधिकार विवाद (ज़मींदारी अधिकार, सुरक्षा) भारत के अन्य हिस्सों में शिकायत थी — जैसे बंगाल के किसान आंदोलन। खेड़ा का मुद्दा वित्तीय था, न कि अधिकार संबंधी।
• विकल्प (c) — सही: खेड़ा की केंद्रीय और विशिष्ट शिकायत औपनिवेशिक सरकार की फसल खराबी के बावजूद पूर्ण भूमि राजस्व वसूलने की जिद थी। किसानों का तर्क था कि उनकी उपज कानूनी रूप से निर्धारित एक-चौथाई छूट सीमा से नीचे गिर गई थी। यह औपनिवेशिक राज्य के साथ एक वित्तीय-प्रशासनिक विवाद था।
• विकल्प (d) — गलत: सिंचाई जल शुल्क दक्कन और अन्य संदर्भों में मुद्दा था — खेड़ा का विवाद नहीं।

• 'राजस्व विवाद (खेड़ा) बनाम कृषि अनुबंध विवाद (चंपारण)' का भेद सबसे महत्वपूर्ण खेड़ा तथ्य है।
• खेड़ा की शिकायत विशेष रूप से भूमि राजस्व समाप्त करने के बारे में नहीं थी — यह मौजूदा छूट नियम के सही लागू करने के बारे में थी।
